analysis.one_liner: Nestle India makes and sells packaged foods and beverages - Maggi noodles, Nescafe, KitKat, baby food and dairy products - and is majority owned by Swiss parent Nestle S.A.
analysis.whats_happening: Nestle India reported Q2 FY27 results on 15 October 2026 (standalone PAT up 36.3% YoY to about Rs 1,027 crore, revenue up 20.3% to Rs 6,788 crore, EBITDA margin 23.8% vs roughly 21.8% a year ago), following a strong Q1 FY27 (revenue up ~25%, PAT up ~48%, margin 24.2% vs 21.6%). Despite the beat, the stock reportedly fell as much as 9% intraday on results day as management flagged rising commodity costs; note the verified price data supplied here is dated 14 October, the day before this move, so the quoted last close does not yet reflect it. One source cited a much larger consolidated profit figure (~Rs 1,968 crore, +41%) that does not match the cluster of other reports and has been set aside as an outlier.
analysis.plain_terms: The headline numbers look good - profit and revenue both growing at double-digit rates for two quarters running, and margins expanding rather than shrinking. The catch is twofold: India cut GST rates on most packaged food in September 2025, which distorts how this year's revenue compares with last year's (trade destocking/restocking swings, not just more product sold), and investors sold the stock anyway on results day because management warned about rising input costs. So the tension is between a genuinely strong quarter and a market that is worried about what happens to margins next.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): revenue ~Rs 6,378 crore (+25% YoY), standalone PAT ~Rs 958-975 crore (+~48%), EBITDA margin 24.2% vs 21.6% a year earlier - management attributed growth to broad-based, volume-led demand. Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): revenue Rs 6,788 crore (+20.3%), standalone PAT Rs 1,027 crore (+36.3%), EBITDA Rs 1,615 crore (+31.1%), margin 23.8%. Flag: since ~85-90% of the portfolio (excluding dairy) saw a GST rate cut from 22 September 2025, these YoY comparisons are not strictly like-for-like - part of the reported growth reflects price/mix shifts and trade destocking/restocking rather than pure volume gains, though the company maintains volumes were double-digit in both quarters.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is 10.2% below its August 2026 peak of Rs 1,540 but is not in crash territory - it sits within its 52-week range (Rs 1,161-1,540) and has actually outperformed both the Nifty and peer Britannia over 1, 3 and 5 years (1Y +18.9% vs Nifty -10.0% and peer -13.6%; 5Y +51.3% vs Nifty +23.4% and peer +36.6%). Two stock splits (10:1 in Jan 2024, 2:1 in Aug 2025) have already been adjusted for in this price series, so the long-run comparison is clean - there is no hidden corporate-action distortion here.
analysis.valuation_read: Nestle India trades at a P/E of roughly 75x and P/B of roughly 46x, far above the broader packaged-foods industry median P/E of around 23x. Why it is expensive: ROE of roughly 68-76% and ROCE of roughly 98% are among the highest of any large listed Indian company, reflecting pricing power, an asset-light model and near-monopoly brands in several categories. Whether that justifies the price is a separate question - the market's ~9% sell-off on a quarter that beat estimates suggests investors are pricing in near-perfect execution, and any margin disappointment from commodity inflation could compress the multiple quickly.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently both volume-led and margin-led, which is unusual and worth noting - management reported double-digit volume growth in both of the last two quarters alongside roughly 200 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion each quarter. The caveat is that the GST rate cut and related trade destocking/restocking make the next one to two quarters' YoY comparisons noisy, so it will take a couple more quarters to see the 'clean' underlying growth rate once the base normalises.
analysis.health_read: Leverage is very low (debt-to-equity reported around 0.09) and the company has historically converted most of its profit into dividends, consistent with profits turning into real cash rather than paper earnings. One search result cited a FY26 free cash flow figure of roughly Rs 42,179 crore, which is implausible given the company's annual revenue base of roughly Rs 25,000-27,000 crore - not verified, check on Screener directly rather than relying on that number. The more relevant risk here is business risk (input cost inflation, regulatory/food-safety scrutiny) rather than financial/balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Nestle S.A. (Switzerland) holds 62.76% with zero pledged shares as of mid-2026, indicating a stable, committed controlling shareholder. The remaining float is split across FIIs (~9.8%), insurance (~7.0%), mutual funds (~4.1%), DIIs (~0.7%) and retail (~15.7%) - there is no well-known individual value investor on the register to flag either way; this is an institutionally and promoter-held stock rather than one followed by star retail investors.
strengths: ROE of roughly 68-76% and ROCE of roughly 98%, among the highest of any large Indian listed company, reflecting brand and pricing power
EBITDA margin expanded by roughly 200 basis points YoY in both Q1 FY27 (24.2% vs 21.6%) and Q2 FY27 (23.8% vs ~21.8%), alongside double-digit volume growth
Very low leverage (debt-to-equity ~0.09) and a stable 62.76% promoter stake with zero pledged shares
Outperformed both the Nifty and peer Britannia over 1, 3 and 5 years (5Y: +51.3% vs Nifty +23.4%, peer +36.6%)
watchpoints: Valuation is stretched at ~75x P/E and ~46x P/B versus an industry median P/E of roughly 23x, leaving little room for error - the stock reportedly fell ~9% intraday on results day despite a profit beat, on commodity cost concerns
GST rate cuts effective 22 September 2025 touched ~85-90% of the portfolio (ex-dairy), making YoY revenue comparisons for the next few quarters noisy due to trade destocking/restocking effects

Regulatory overhang: FSSAI flagged a low-fat dairy whitener sample as unsafe/substandard (3 October 2026) and filed adjudication cases over infant-nutrition products (18 September 2026) - a reputational risk for a business whose pricing power rests on consumer trust
CFO transition under way - Svetlana Boldina steps down (effective 31 January 2026), succeeded by Edouard Mac Nab - amid a broader wave of leadership changes across Indian FMCG peers (HUL, Britannia)
analysis.one_thing: Whether the EBITDA margin (23.8% in Q2 FY27) holds or compresses over the next one to two quarters as the commodity cost inflation management flagged on the Q2 call works through the P&L - that is what will determine whether the current premium valuation is sustainable.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 and Q2 FY27 revenue, PAT and EBITDA margin figures were cross-checked across multiple independent outlets (freepressjournal, inkl, whalesbook, indiainfoline, kotakneo) which converge; one outlier (apacnewsnetwork's 'Rs 1,968 crore consolidated profit, +41%') did not match this cluster and was set aside rather than averaged in, per sourcing policy. Valuation and profitability ratios (P/E ~75x, P/B ~46x, ROE ~68-76%, ROCE ~98%) were cross-checked across eulerpool, valueresearch and marketsmojo commentary. A FY26 free-cash-flow figure of Rs 42,179 crore surfaced in one aggregator search snippet but is implausible against Nestle India's revenue base and was excluded - not verified, check on Screener. Promoter holding (62.76%, zero pledge) was cross-checked across choiceindia and arthneeti. Supplied market-data snapshot is dated 14 October 2026, one day before the Q2 results and reported post-results stock drop, so price-based figures here predate that move.
